shortTitle: Use cases and build vs buy
title: Choosing use cases, and build versus buy
hook: Scoring ideas, piloting against a baseline, measuring value, and deciding to buy, build or blend.
inPlainWords: Most failed AI projects fail before any model is built. The problem was wrong, the value was never measured, or the team built what it could have bought. This stop is the checklist for that decision.

useCase.title: ShopEase has 12 AI ideas and one small team
useCase.story: Ideas include the support bot, return prediction, fraud alerts, product descriptions, demand forecasting, a voice assistant and more. There is budget for two projects this quarter. Which two, and should ShopEase build or buy?

approaches.name: Score ideas by value and feasibility
approaches.what: Rate each idea on business value, data readiness, risk and effort.
approaches.example: Support bot: high value, ready data, medium risk.

approaches.name: Pilot against a baseline
approaches.what: Test on a small slice and compare with the current process.
approaches.example: The bot handles 10% of tickets and is compared with human agents.

approaches.name: Measure the business result
approaches.what: Tie the project to a number the business already tracks.
approaches.example: Hours saved, cost per ticket, returns avoided.

approaches.name: Buy a ready product
approaches.what: Use a finished product or service.
approaches.greatWhen: A common problem that others have already solved.
approaches.avoidWhen: Your edge depends on it, or the product cannot fit your data or rules.

approaches.name: Build with existing parts
approaches.what: Assemble your own from models, search and tools.
approaches.greatWhen: A specific need that no product meets.
approaches.avoidWhen: You lack a team to run it.
approaches.example: A custom assistant that uses your policies and order system.

approaches.name: Blend: buy the common, build the edge
approaches.what: Buy the standard parts and build only where you differ.
approaches.avoidWhen: Nobody owns the seams between the parts.
approaches.example: Buy speech to text, build the refund workflow.

approaches.name: Total cost and an exit plan
approaches.what: Count build cost, running cost, review time and the cost of switching.
approaches.example: Include monitoring and human review time.

challenge.question: Two project slots and a small team. What is the smartest approach?

options.text: Score ideas on value, data readiness and risk. Pilot two against a baseline, measure business results, buy common parts, and build only what is different
options.why: It picks by evidence, proves it small, and spends build effort where it matters.
Technology is not a problem to solve.

options.text: Build everything in-house to stay independent
options.why: You will spend the quarter rebuilding what already exists.

options.text: Buy something for every idea, with no pilot
options.why: Fast, but you do not learn if it works for you.

bestCase.title: Choose by value and readiness, prove it small, buy the common parts
bestCase.example: ShopEase picks the support bot and return prediction: high value, data ready, moderate risk. Each runs a pilot against today's process. They buy speech to text and a monitoring tool, and build the refund workflow that is unique to the store. Results are reported in hours saved and returns avoided.

worstCase.title: Starting from the technology, not the problem
worstCase.example: The team builds a flashy voice assistant nobody asked for, in-house, with no baseline. After six months it handles 2% of calls, costs more than the human team, and is quietly shelved.

route.travelling: Idea list: 12 AI ideas and 2 slots

steps.label: Score value, data and risk
steps.goes: The support bot and return prediction rank highest.
steps.goesWrong: The most exciting technology is picked without scoring.

steps.label: Pilot against a baseline
steps.goes: Each runs on a small slice and is compared with today's process.

steps.label: Buy, build or blend
steps.goes: Buy common parts. Build what makes ShopEase different.

steps.label: Measure business results
steps.goes: Track hours saved and returns avoided.

takeaway: Pick problems by value and readiness, prove them small, and buy what is common. Build only what makes you different.
